title: A renewal rule written for 90-day certificates renews 45-day ones twice as often

cases.name: Certificate lifetime: 90 days · Renewal rule: Certbot 4.1+ default

steps.title: Public certificates shrink from 398 days to 47
steps.line: 398 days, then 200 from 2026, 100 from 2027 and 47 from 2029.
steps.caption: The CA/Browser Forum’s Baseline Requirements cap how long a publicly trusted TLS certificate may be valid. The cap was 398 days until 15 March 2026 and 200 days from then. It falls to 100 days in March 2027 and to 47 in March 2029. When the lifetime shrinks, does a rule that renews 30 days before expiry still leave enough time between certificates? We will compare it with a rule tied to the certificate’s lifetime.
steps.picture: Timeline “Longest a public TLS certificate may last”: 4 periods.

steps.title: Let’s Encrypt’s default reaches 45 days in 2028
steps.line: The classic profile: 90 days, then 64 from 2027 and 45 from 2028.
steps.caption: The same timeline, edited to Let’s Encrypt’s schedule. Its opt-in tlsserver profile has issued 45-day certificates since May 2026. The default classic profile issues 90-day certificates until February 2027, then 64-day ones, and 45-day ones from February 2028, a year before the 47-day cap.
steps.picture: Timeline “Let’s Encrypt’s certificate lifetimes”: 4 periods.

steps.title: Certbot 3.3 renews 30 days before expiry
steps.line: A 90-day certificate is replaced by the run at day 60.
steps.caption: Certbot 3.3 renews when the certificate expires within renew_before_expiry, 30 days unless the renewal file sets it. Let’s Encrypt dates a certificate 58.5 minutes before it issues it, so a 90-day one falls due just before the run at day 60, which replaces it.

steps.title: Certbot 4.1 renews two thirds of the way through
steps.line: Two thirds of 90 days is day 60; the replacement does not move.
steps.caption: Since 4.1, with renew_before_expiry unset and no ARI answer, Certbot renews two thirds of the way through a certificate’s life, or half way for certificates shorter than ten days. Two thirds of 90 days is day 60, the day the old rule chose, so for 90-day certificates nothing moved.

steps.title: Certbot’s renewals still count against the limit
steps.line: Certbot’s order names no predecessor, so the limit check runs.
steps.caption: More frequent renewals matter if they consume an issuance limit. Boulder skips the 5-in-7-days check only for an order that names the certificate it replaces and arrives inside that certificate’s window. Certbot 5.8’s order carries identifiers and a profile, nothing more, so every renewal is checked. A refused order costs nothing; an issued certificate takes a token.

cases.name: Certificate lifetime: 160 hours · Renewal rule: 30 days before expiry

steps.title: Public certificates shrink from 398 days to 47
steps.line: 398 days, then 200 from 2026, 100 from 2027 and 47 from 2029.
steps.caption: The CA/Browser Forum’s Baseline Requirements cap how long a publicly trusted TLS certificate may be valid. The cap was 398 days until 15 March 2026 and 200 days from then. It falls to 100 days in March 2027 and to 47 in March 2029. When the lifetime shrinks, does a rule that renews 30 days before expiry still leave enough time between certificates? We will compare it with a rule tied to the certificate’s lifetime.
steps.picture: Timeline “Longest a public TLS certificate may last”: 4 periods.

steps.title: Let’s Encrypt’s default reaches 45 days in 2028
steps.line: The classic profile: 90 days, then 64 from 2027 and 45 from 2028.
steps.caption: The same timeline, edited to Let’s Encrypt’s schedule. Its opt-in tlsserver profile has issued 45-day certificates since May 2026. The default classic profile issues 90-day certificates until February 2027, then 64-day ones, and 45-day ones from February 2028, a year before the 47-day cap.
steps.picture: Timeline “Let’s Encrypt’s certificate lifetimes”: 4 periods.

steps.title: Certbot 3.3 renews 30 days before expiry
steps.line: A 90-day certificate is replaced by the run at day 60.
steps.caption: Certbot 3.3 renews when the certificate expires within renew_before_expiry, 30 days unless the renewal file sets it. Let’s Encrypt dates a certificate 58.5 minutes before it issues it, so a 90-day one falls due just before the run at day 60, which replaces it.

steps.title: Certbot 4.1 renews two thirds of the way through
steps.line: Two thirds of 90 days is day 60; the replacement does not move.
steps.caption: Since 4.1, with renew_before_expiry unset and no ARI answer, Certbot renews two thirds of the way through a certificate’s life, or half way for certificates shorter than ten days. Two thirds of 90 days is day 60, the day the old rule chose, so for 90-day certificates nothing moved.
